_doc: Findings a human has accepted for this release, each naming its card.
The smoke report is EVIDENCE and is never edited to make a gate pass. This
file is the separate, reviewable record of which findings were triaged and
consciously shipped with - so the acceptance is auditable, attributable and
sits next to the evidence rather than inside it.
The release skill's own rule: a pre-existing finding 'does not block - it
gets a card and a line in the audit file, so the delta stays honest'.
Rules the gate enforces, so this cannot become a dumping ground:
- every entry names a real card id and a reason;
- every entry names the version it is accepted FOR, and is ignored for any
other version, so an acceptance cannot silently carry forward;
- a finding in the report that is NOT listed here still blocks.
Accepting a finding is a decision someone made. Removing an entry is how you
`resolved` is NOT `accepted`. An accepted finding ships as-is. A resolved one
was FIXED after the walk recorded it, so the report is simply stale for that
entry - and the honest answer to a stale report is a re-walk. Where a re-walk
was not run, the entry must say exactly how the fix was verified instead, so a
reader can weigh that evidence rather than assume a walk covered it.

accepted.reason: Environment, not code. wp wpss preflight counts every historical fatal in wss.local's debug.log (oldest 03-Sep), and the entries come from contract-test runs and ad-hoc eval. No fatal came from the browser flows of this walk.

Test hygiene. The test assumes service moderation is off; on this site it is on, so its publish is forced to pending and the price lookup returns WP_Error. The add-on pricing code path is untouched in 1.8.0, and the other 94 Free contract scripts pass.

Pre-existing and environment-driven. EarningsController already rounds to 2 places, unchanged since v1.7.2. The trailing digits appear only because wss.local's php.ini sets serialize_precision=17 instead of PHP's default -1, verified with wp_json_encode(round(113.4,2)). The _minor integer beside the field is exact.
Test hygiene. Fixture teardown SQL names columns that no longer exist, so test rows are left behind on the dev site. It does not ship to customers and is not a plugin runtime path.

Pre-existing since v1.7.2: RequirementsService::process_uploads() skips a file that wpss_check_upload() refuses, without telling the buyer. The file input's accept list stops this in normal use; the walk reached it only by forcing a .txt in with setInputFiles. The allowed files on the same submission save correctly.

debug_log_accepted.reason: Log output of TESTS-cleanup-sql-stale-columns: the contract suite's teardown SQL, not plugin runtime.

Nine wpdb::prepare notices that recur when the full contract suite runs (seen in both the combo and free walks). They did not appear when each script was run alone, and no browser flow emitted one in either walk. The caller is not yet identified; tracked on the card.

debug_log_accepted.match: Cannot use object of type WP_Error as array
debug_log_accepted.reason: Log output of TEST-addon-pricing-contract-fatal, raised inside the test script (eval line 64), not plugin code.

Environment: an earlier test left the wpss_active_storage_provider option set to a provider that does not exist. The plugin correctly logs the problem and falls back to local disk, and every upload in the walk succeeded.

debug_log_accepted.match: No fatal, warning or deprecated from plugin code
debug_log_accepted.reason: Not a defect: this is the walker's note that the browser-flow window was clean. The money lines it mentions are deliberate refusal logging from contract-suite fixtures.
Third-party dev plugin (woo-order-test) PHP 8.2 dynamic-property deprecations, emitted on every boot. Not WPSS code.
Log output of TEST-addon-pricing-contract-fatal, inside the test's own eval, not plugin runtime.

Deliberate refund-guard refusals driven by contract-suite fixtures (offline rail, already-settled charge, partial refund). The system is correctly refusing and announcing a skipped money step; none came from the browser flows.

coverage_verified_elsewhere.verified_by: A scripted upgrade cycle in the docker-smoke stack, not a browser walk. WordPress 6.9 + PHP 8.3, clean DB: install the PUBLISHED v1.7.1 free and pro ZIPs and activate; seed a vendor, a buyer, a published service at 120 and that buyer's one-item cart; deactivate both and wind wpss_db_version back to 1.6.0 so install() has a real migration to run; then overwrite both plugins with the built 1.7.2 ZIPs (wp plugin install --force, the path the updater takes), reactivate, and load the site. Result: free 1.7.2 / pro 1.7.2, both active, frontend 200, wpss_db_version 1.6.0 -> 1.7.3, 28 tables (no loss), the service count unchanged, the buyer's cart still 1 item at 120 and the service still published, and zero Fatal / Uncaught / textdomain lines in debug.log across the whole cycle.
coverage_verified_elsewhere.evidence: scratchpad/docker-upgrade-test.sh - rerunnable; prints each assertion and exits non-zero on any failure.
coverage_verified_elsewhere.note: The free walk could not run this section: its own prompt forbade deactivating or activating plugins, which an upgrade cycle requires, so all three of its checks recorded as skipped. That is a limit of how the walk was commissioned, not of the product - the right answer is to run the cycle somewhere it is allowed and say exactly what was run, which is what this entry is. It is weaker than a walk in one specific way: it asserts on data and logs, not on what a buyer or owner SEES after an upgrade.

staleness.state: The recorded COMBO walk (9b0909ec) is stale: ten rendered files changed after it ran. Both release builds were taken with --force.
staleness.why_not_a_re-walk: Six of those ten files changed BECAUSE of what a walk found after 9b0909ec, and each change was verified against the behaviour it touches rather than by re-running a 40-minute walk that would itself be stale by the next fix. The evidence per fix is in `resolved` above, and each entry says in writing how it was verified and that it was not a walk.
staleness.what_was_walked_after_the_recorded_run: A free-mode walk (f5e767cc, docs/qa/.last-smoke-pass-free.json) and a scoped combo-mode browser walk covering exactly the three surfaces the first six file changes render - the cart on both rails at 1280 and 390, Settings > Advanced, and a vendor editing their own service through the dashboard. That scoped walk is what found the checkout defect a direct probe of the cart reader had missed, which is the strongest argument in this file for why a browser walk is not interchangeable with a probe.
staleness.verified_on_the_built_artifacts: Pristine install of both 1.7.2 ZIPs on clean WordPress + PHP 8.3: both active, frontend 200, 28 tables, zero fatals, production autoloader. Upgrade 1.7.1 -> 1.7.2 with wpss_db_version wound back to 1.6.0 so the migration ran: schema 1.6.0 -> 1.7.3, no table loss, an existing buyer's cart and service unchanged, zero fatals. Both re-run against the final ZIPs, not an earlier build.
staleness.not_covered: No full combo walk describes the shipped tree. The surfaces changed after the scoped walk are src/Core/Plugin.php (an upgrade migration, covered by the upgrade cycle above) and the four cart/checkout files (covered by the probes in `resolved`). What none of this covers is the rest of the product as a whole at the shipped commit - a full combo walk is the first thing 1.7.3 should do, before any change.
